results.name: correlated_math_trap_department_salary
results.anti_pattern: The Correlated Math Trap: Quadratic correlated subquery calculating department average salary in WHERE clause
results.original_query: SELECT e.id, e.name, e.department_id, e.salary,        (SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM employees e2 WHERE e2.department_id = e.department_id) AS dept_avg_salary FROM employees e WHERE e.salary > (     SELECT AVG(e3.salary) * 1.15     FROM employees e3     WHERE e3.department_id = e.department_id ) ORDER BY e.salary DESC;
results.optimized_sql:
WITH dept_stats AS (
    SELECT id, name, department_id, salary,
           AVG(salary) OVER(PARTITION BY department_id) AS dept_avg_salary
    FROM employees
)
SELECT id, name, department_id, salary, dept_avg_salary
FROM dept_stats
WHERE salary > (dept_avg_salary * 1.15)
ORDER BY salary DESC;
results.verification_message: Result sets match perfectly as multiset (1411 rows).
results.raw_llm_response:
```sql
WITH dept_stats AS (

)
```

results.name: top_record_tie_trap_max_salary

results.optimized_sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT id, department_id, salary,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rn
    FROM employees
)
SELECT id, department_id, salary
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1;
